children: New Delhi, Nov. 15 -- Nvidia, the second-most valuable company in the world, is in the process of finding its new CEO after Jensen Huang, the only person who has led the chipmaker since its founding in 1993, was forced to step down amid a series of allegations of extramarital affairs. Colette Kress, who until now served as the company's Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, has been appointed as the interim CEO, while the board continues to search for a permanent executive to lead the $4 trillion giant.

Over the past few days, several names, including both insiders and outsiders who hold leadership roles in top companies, have been discussed for the role. Among them is Thomas Kurian, who is currently the CEO of Google cloud.

Born in Kerala's Kottayam in 1966 as one of the four children of PC Kurian, a chemical engineer and the general manager of Graphite India, and his wife, Molly, Thomas did his schooling in Bangalore and later joined IIT Madras.

At the age of 17, Thomas, along with his identical twin brother George Kurian, moved to the US, where he graduated from Princeton with a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering. He also has an MBA from the Stanford Graduate School of Business.
Kurian started his career as a management consultant at McKinsey & Company from 1990 to 1996, working as a business analyst and engagement manager.

Kurian joined Oracle in 1996, and in the 22 years there he rose to become President of Product Development and oversaw a multibillion-dollar R&D budget. He resigned in September 2018 following strategic disagreements with co-founder Larry Ellison over cloud computing.

Two months later, in November 2018, he joined Google, where he currently serves as the CEO of Google Cloud. Kurian has been ranked among the top-earning technology executives in the US and currently is estimated to be worth $ 1.8 billion depending on Alphabet stock performance.
His identical twin brother George, who also followed Thomas to the US, is currently the CEO of NetApp.

Meanwhile, as uncertainty continues inside Nvidia, more than 1.32 lakh people have signed an online petition urging the company's board to reinstate Huang as chief executive. The campaign has also attracted support from prominent technology industry figures, including Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.
